clue.text: Primate hot, to a degree, wearing fur hat

indicators.note: the hat is worn around the other letters, so it contains them

parts.note: a busby is the tall fur hat of a hussar or guardsman
H is the abbreviation for hot on taps
BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a degree

explanation.surface: A monkey, rather warm, is sporting a furry hat.
explanation.definitionFit: The bushbaby, or galago, is a small nocturnal African primate with big eyes.

clue.text: Ugly women's trousers

definitions.meaning: a slang insult for unattractive women
Oxford ... are wide trousers, so ... means trousers

explanation.surface: Unattractive women's slacks.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a crude slang term for unattractive women and a British word for loose trousers.

clue.text: Picture game

definitions.meaning: a card game where players call out on matching cards

explanation.definitionFit: A snap is a quick photograph and also a children's card game.

clue.text: Most advantageous to secure just the most intelligent

indicators.note: the outer word holds the other safely inside

explanation.surface: The best course is to secure only the cleverest people.
explanation.definitionFit: Brightest is a superlative of bright, clever, so it means most intelligent.

clue.text: Corner one at Aintree to have a drink

parts.note: the Elbow is a famous bend on the Grand National course at Aintree racecourse

explanation.surface: Rounding a turn at Aintree racecourse, then stopping for a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Aintree, near Liverpool, hosts the Grand National steeplechase; the Elbow is the turn before its run-in.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes raising a glass to the lips, so it means to drink alcohol.

clue.text: Gosh, not much of a bloomer!

definitions.meaning: an exclamation of surprise, like 'blimey' or 'goodness'
a bloomer is a crusty British loaf, and only tiny bits of one would be little of it

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims at a very minor blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' reads as a mistake, but here it is a British loaf of bread.
explanation.definitionFit: The word works both as a mild exclamation of surprise and as small fragments left from bread.

clue.text: Man in pub's shown up — as this didn't work?

indicators.note: in a down entry 'up' means the letters are read from bottom to top
the man's word sits inside the pub

explanation.surface: A man in the pub is shown up, as if his treatment failed.
explanation.walkthrough: BAHER read upwards gives the answer; the definition hints at a treatment that someone refused or relapsed after.
explanation.definitionFit: Rehabilitation treatment for addicts is what the clue suggests had no effect.

clue.text: Island where bird has feeling of resentment, made to go topless

parts.note: a martin is a bird of the swallow family

indicators.note: the first letter of the resentment word is removed, its top in a down entry

explanation.surface: On an island, a bird is resentful at being forced to sunbathe topless.
explanation.definitionFit: Martinique is a French Caribbean island.

clue.text: Egotist wishing to find himself?

parts.note: read literally, someone who seeks the self, a person searching for his own identity

explanation.definitionFit: A self-centred person pursuing his own interest is an egotist.

clue.text: Bank given permit about to expire

indicators.note: one word goes round the other, as 'about' means surrounding

explanation.surface: A bank is issued a licence that is about to lapse.
explanation.definitionFit: A bank in the sense of a slope or incline, which a gradient also is.

clue.text: Husband is in the pink in such harmonious society

indicators.note: the husband's letter is placed inside the colour word

parts.note: coral is a shade of pink

explanation.surface: A husband in fine health thrives in a congenial social circle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the pink' looks like the idiom for healthy, but 'the pink' is the colour CORAL; 'such' makes the definition adjectival, describing a singing society.
explanation.definitionFit: A choral society is a group that sings together in harmony, so the adjective describes that kind of club.

clue.text: Flight attendant yet to turn up carrying bread, an easy catch

indicators.note: the reversed word holds the bread inside
in a down entry the word is turned to read upwards

parts.note: a dolly is an easy catch in cricket

explanation.surface: A flight attendant has yet to come up with bread, an easy catch.
explanation.walkthrough: TEY carries ROLL; dolly is cricket slang for a simple catch.
explanation.definitionFit: Trolley dolly is British slang for an air steward pushing a drinks cart.

clue.text: Piece stripped back —- fragments said to be lucky?

parts.note: a whit is a tiny piece, as in 'not a whit'

indicators.note: the word for stripped is read backwards

explanation.surface: A piece is stripped back to fragments that people consider good luck.
explanation.walkthrough: Saying the phrase on the first day of a month is a British superstition supposed to bring luck.
explanation.definitionFit: The words are a traditional good-luck charm uttered at the start of each month.

clue.text: Torrent of abuse upsetting Serbian hag

indicators.note: overturning the words mixes their letters

explanation.surface: A Serbian old woman upset by a stream of insults.
explanation.definitionFit: Ear-bashing is British slang for a prolonged scolding or harangue.

clue.text: Offered notes on girls in summer wear

indicators.note: in a down entry the first piece sits on top of the second

explanation.surface: Musical notes were offered to girls dressed for summer.
explanation.definitionFit: Sunglasses are eyewear typically worn in summer.

clue.text: A sweet that's sharp

parts.note: sweet in the sense of endearing, cute

explanation.surface: A sweet that tastes tangy.
explanation.definitionFit: Acute and sharp are synonyms, as for a pain or a mind.

clue.text: Plant first of trees in square after devastating gale

indicators.note: the piece built from the square comes after the scrambled gale
a gale wreaking havoc scatters its own letters
the tree's initial goes inside the square number

parts.note: nine is a square number, three times three

indicators.note: only the opening letter of trees is taken

explanation.surface: A plant comes first among trees in the square after a fierce storm.
explanation.walkthrough: The square is a number squared, here three times three, a convention the solver may not expect; 'devastating' signals the scrambling of the storm word.
explanation.definitionFit: Eglantine is the sweetbriar, a wild rose plant.

clue.text: Suggests the state of Minnesota?

indicators.note: the condition the letters are in, a jumbled state

explanation.surface: A question about what Minnesota's state proposes.
explanation.definitionFit: To nominate is to put forward or suggest a candidate.

clue.text: Lovely carrying a gun, as light piece

indicators.note: the beauty holds the other letters inside

parts.note: a lovely is a beautiful woman, a belle
gat is slang for a gun

explanation.surface: A beautiful woman is toting a firearm, as in a light-hearted film.
explanation.definitionFit: A bagatelle is a short, light piece of music, especially for piano.

clue.text: Computer accessory has second function

parts.note: mo is a moment, a second

explanation.surface: A computer peripheral has a secondary role.
explanation.definitionFit: The handheld pointing device is a standard computer accessory.

clue.text: Having thrashed Holland, smiling —- not at home, one's own patch

indicators.note: beating the words up mixes their letters

parts.note: being in means being at home

explanation.surface: After beating Holland, a happy team is no longer on home ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes IN from the pooled letters of HOLLAND and SMILING; the rest is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A smallholding is a small farm, a person's own patch of land.

clue.text: Pointed instrument pressing name into material

indicators.note: the name's letter is pressed inside the fabric

explanation.surface: A sharp tool pressing a name into cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: A lance is a long pointed weapon or a surgical lancet.

clue.text: On a date, nothing's pinched!

indicators.note: the letters are pinched, taken from within the phrase

explanation.surface: On a date, nothing was stolen.
explanation.definitionFit: Nada is Spanish for nothing, used colloquially in English.

clue.text: Spent some time on the radio

indicators.note: broadcast speech is heard rather than read

parts.note: a week is a period of time

explanation.surface: Someone spent a while broadcasting.
explanation.definitionFit: Spent means exhausted, so weak.

clue.text: Lacking sensible thought, nursing sickness in the head?

definitions.text: Lacking sensible thought, nursing sickness in the head?

indicators.note: the word for silly holds the letter, as a nurse cradles a baby
the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone without sense is harbouring a mental illness.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole clue describes madness: senseless and sick in the head.

clue.text: Dull game's ending for fellow resident

parts.note: mate, checkmate, ends a chess game

explanation.surface: A dreary game finish for someone who lives with you.
explanation.definitionFit: A flatmate is someone sharing a flat, a fellow resident.

clue.text: One's very emotional at evidence of oil strike

definitions.meaning: a person who gushes, effusive in feeling
a well spouting oil shows drillers have hit it

explanation.surface: Someone gets emotional on seeing oil come up.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an effusive person and an oil well that spouts freely.

clue.text: Part of a lobster certainly, say, put on back of plate

indicators.note: in an across entry the following words are placed after that letter
only the closing letter of plate is taken

explanation.surface: Certainly, say, something served on the back of a plate is part of a lobster.
explanation.definitionFit: A lobster's eyes sit on movable stalks, one of its body parts.
